## PostgreSQL serialization and invariants

A prospective PostgreSQL writer uses a per-chain `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` lock as the normative minimum; global locking is prohibited. Database constraints, uniqueness, foreign keys, immutable-entry privileges/triggers, byte-length checks, sequence/head/count consistency, and idempotency receipt invariants are part of the correctness proof. `SERIALIZABLE` may be used defensively but is not required to replace the per-chain lock and invariants.
## Concurrency invariants

Per-chain row locking with `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`, plus the stated database invariants, is the normative minimum. `SERIALIZABLE` may be used as a defensive or measured profile, but it does not replace the per-chain lock and invariants. Independent chains MUST NOT be globally serialized. Revocation and kill changes use the same authority-domain serialization boundary so an append cannot commit across an effective boundary.
